name: How do I know if my renovation needs structural engineering?

mainEntity.name: When does a home renovation need a structural engineer in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: When does a home renovation need a structural engineer in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: A renovation usually needs structural engineering whenever the work changes how the home carries weight. That includes removing or modifying load-bearing walls, adding openings, expanding the house, changing roof framing, altering foundations, or building over garages or other existing structures. In Los Angeles, engineering is also common for older homes, hillside sites, and projects with irregular framing. Homeowners often underestimate this step because structural problems are not always visible. A wall that looks easy to remove may carry significant load, and that can affect both cost and permit review. Engineering should be addressed during planning, not after demolition starts. If the project might involve beams, posts, footings, or lateral upgrades, a structural engineer should review the design early so the drawings and construction plan stay aligned. This avoids rework, delays, and inspection issues later.
acceptedAnswer.description: A structural engineer is usually needed when a renovation affects load-bearing walls, foundations, roof framing, beams, additions, or major openings. If the project changes how weight is carried through the home, engineering is typically required for safe design and permitting.
